Déterminer pourquoi elles n'ont pas été exécutées, vérifier les autorisations et les budgets disponibles, corriger les défauts internes lorsque c'est autorisé, puis poursuivre les stratégies réalisables. q1_whatAreTheEight.answer: The 'eight' are the 8 TRIALS of scenario J (4 tasks × 2 trials). Each trial ran TWO strategies — a default and one rule-selected alternative — so 8 alternative-strategy executions exist (6 DECOMPOSED_INTERMEDIATE_VERIFICATION + 2 LARGER_MODEL_REPAIR_DEPTH), and each trial ended with 1 sovereign-delegation record (8 total). The 8 alternatives WERE executed (executionStatus EXECUTED, sandboxed) and all failed. What was NOT executed are the 8 delegation records (state CREATED, never AUTHORIZED, 0 provider calls). 'Not executed' therefore applies to the provider handoffs, not to the local strategies.

REPAIR_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED_semantics.fact: buildProject sets repairStopReason REPAIR_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED when the loop ends unverified with repairs >= maxRepair; maxRepair = Number(deps.maxRepair) || 1. With maxRepair 1 it means: first pass failed, ONE repair round regenerated the files with the failure hint, still failed. It is an internal compute bound (repair rounds), NOT money and NOT an authorization.
REPAIR_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED_semantics.pointer: runtime/core/native-project-builder.ts buildProject: `const maxRepair = Number(deps.maxRepair) || 1;` and `if (repairStopReason === null && !(build.ok && verified) && repairs >= maxRepair && maxRepair > 0) repairStopReason = "REPAIR_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED";`

NO_PROGRESS_semantics.fact: NO_PROGRESS_IDENTICAL_REGENERATION fires when every file regenerated successfully AND the snapshot is byte-identical to the previous round (an identical retry carries no information at temperature 0).
NO_PROGRESS_semantics.pointer: runtime/core/native-project-builder.ts buildProject anti-loop (`if (regenFailed === 0 && snapshot() === before) { repairStopReason = "NO_PROGRESS_IDENTICAL_REGENERATION"; break; }`)

rootCauses.title: The default arm was a PROBE, not a capability attempt
rootCauses.detail: The policy had no CALIBRATED evidence for implement ⇒ tier PROBE (3b, maxRepair 1). The V15.9 measured overlay (NO_QUALIFIED_LOCAL_MODEL) sets escalateIfStillFails=true but by design NEVER changes maxRepair/tier. So the 8 default stops are 'one cheap repair failed', and the escalation decision is taken after a probe-sized local budget.
pointers: docs/odg/evidence/V161_SCENARIO_J.json#rows[*].policy (tier PROBE, maxRepair 1, measuredDecision NO_QUALIFIED_LOCAL_MODEL, escalateIfStillFails true)

runtime/core/odg-local-model-execution-policy.ts chooseExecutionPolicy (PROBE branch: 3b, maxRepair 1) and overlay comment '(b) set escalateIfStillFails=true when the class is NO_QUALIFIED_LOCAL_MODEL … maxRepair / tier / quality / pForPlanner are NEVER changed'

rootCauses.title: Single-lever alternatives: the decomposed arm inherited the probe budget
rootCauses.detail: Rule R3 keeps the SAME model and maxRepair as the default (3b, 1); R4 (7b, 3) is only reachable when no intermediate oracle exists. The rules are mutually exclusive and not chained, so for the 3 decomposable tasks the localized failing part (report.js / collect.js) received exactly ONE 3b repair; the max-local tier was never applied to it.

rootCauses.title: Localisation worked; the failures are concentrated on the composing/top file
rootCauses.detail: Across the 6 decomposed runs 8 of the 11 distinct (task,part) sub-problems attempted verified (parse/encode/decode, parse/validate, parse/clamp/flagged); each chain stopped at exactly one part: report.js (rle, range-clamp: 'entry report.js is not a function') or collect.js (csv: 'threw: input.split is not a function').

rootCauses.title: 'entry report.js is not a function' = export-shape error, not logic
rootCauses.detail: The sandbox grader emits this exact message when the observation is `missing` (the loaded entry export is not callable). The report.js contracts read 'Export (s) = { encoded, roundtrip }' / 'Export (s) = { clamped, flaggedCount }', which a 3b model can plausibly read as 'export an object'. Generated sources were NOT retained in the evidence, so this cannot be confirmed from committed data.
pointers: runtime/core/odg-native-build-sandbox.ts gradeCases (`if (o.missing) return { pass:false, error: `case ${i}: entry ${c.entry} is not a function` }`)
rootCauses.confirmBy: J2 retains sha256 + source of every generated file (C6 below)

rootCauses.title: csv collect.js mis-composed the dependency contract
rootCauses.detail: validate.js is specified 'string -> boolean[]'; a collect.js that passes parsed rows (an array) to validate (whose frozen parse.js calls .split on its input) or calls .split on a non-string would throw 'input.split is not a function'. Not confirmable without the generated source.

rootCauses.title: The failing parts got only the GENERIC repair hint
rootCauses.detail: The runner supplies structured repairExamples only when every expected result is primitive (isPrim), because odg-repair-feedback compared with === at the time. report.js/collect.js return objects ⇒ structuredRepairExamples false ⇒ generic 'BUILDS but FAILS' hint. Only encode.js (rle) and flagged.js (range-clamp) — primitive results — got structured examples; encode.js and clamp.js were the parts that recovered after 1 repair (clamp.js without structured examples).

rootCauses.title: parse-range: genuine local plateau at the max-local tier
rootCauses.detail: 7b/maxRepair 3 reached NO_PROGRESS_IDENTICAL_REGENERATION after 2 repairs on the decomposition-planner's generic META split (extract-a/extract-b/f.js, triggered because the contract contains the word 'parse'). The R4 arm deliberately reused that architecture; a single-file 7b attempt was not tried. Whether the generic META split itself hurts is a HYPOTHESIS (V155 registry: all three models 0/3 on the TS form of this task, so the task is hard independently of the split).

q1_effectOfPR940.summary: Neither canonical defect changed J's measured outcome; a re-run of the SAME runner at the current base would, by hypothesis, reproduce 0/8 (temperature 0, seed 42, same prompts).

DEFECT_J1_decomposedExecutionModules.fact: Pre-#940 odg-decomposed-execution threaded only bo.modules, which a SANDBOXED build never returns. The J runner COMPENSATED by freezing verified files through its own generator seam (runDecomposedAlt `gen` serves verified[f.path]); so in J the later sub-problems DID compose on the verified sources. The defect was real in the canonical module but did not affect J's arm.
pointers: runtime/bin/odg-v161-scenario-j-run.ts runDecomposedAlt (`const gen = async (f, bc) => (… hasOwnProperty.call(verified, f.path) ? { ok:true, content: verified[f.path] } : gen0(f, bc))`)

DEFECT_J2_repairFeedbackStrictEq.fact: Pre-#940 buildExecutionFeedback used `actual === ex.expect`. The J runner AVOIDED the defect by never passing structured examples for non-primitive results (RC-6). So J2 did not corrupt any J feedback; it explains WHY the object-returning failing parts got only generic hints. The current runner still contains the isPrim filter, so re-running it unchanged would still give them generic hints.
pointers: runtime/bin/odg-v161-scenario-j-run.ts hardTask() isPrim filter (unchanged at base c6a3df99)

wouldRerunDiffer.answer: NO for an unchanged re-run (deterministic decoding; both canonical fixes were already compensated/avoided by the runner). A DIFFERENT experiment could differ: (a) structured object-result repair examples are now meaningful (structuralEqual), (b) the canonical runDecomposed can now be used without the runner's freezing seam, (c) the failing part could get the max-local tier. That is what J2 tests.

q2_sovereignDelegationRecords.conclusion: The 8 delegation records are PROVIDER handoffs that would consume EXTERNAL spend (provider calls) under an authorization ODG/provider cannot grant itself. They are OWNER-GATED: they need (1) an owner authorization bound to each mission id and (2) a verifiable spend ceiling, which does not exist in the chain today. They are NOT part of the internal repair budget: REPAIR_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED is a count of local repair rounds (€0, loopback Ollama) inside native-project-builder. Raising maxRepair or switching to 7b costs local compute only and needs no spend authorization; executing a delegation record does.

isRevisionJustified.answer: A RETROACTIVE revision to make J pass is NOT justified: it would turn a criterion failure into a pass after seeing the data (post-hoc). J stays EXECUTED_PARTIAL on its own evidence. A FORWARD revision is defensible on substance — REPAIR_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED is also an ODG-decided repetitive-failure stop, and the criterion's intent ('arrête les tentatives répétitives') is served by either stop — but only as a NEW pre-registered criterion for a NEW experiment (J2), decided by the owner/CTO since the contract is PROPOSED and the scenario contracts are governance artefacts.
